title: Seat Belts & Child Restraints
whatItIs: Seat belts must be worn where fitted. The driver is responsible for every child under 14; passengers aged 14 and over are responsible for themselves.

keyFacts.text: You MUST wear a seat belt in a car if one is fitted, unless you are exempt.
The driver MUST make sure every child under 14 is properly belted or restrained.
Under 1.35 m: a child restraint suitable for the child's weight MUST be used.
A rear-facing baby seat MUST NOT be fitted in a seat protected by an active frontal airbag.

keyFacts: No seat belt, or a child under 14 not properly restrained: fine of up to £500.

onTheTest.question: You are driving your 10-year-old, who is 1.30 m tall, in the back of your car. What does the law require?
options: An adult seat belt is enough
Nothing, as rear seats are exempt
A child restraint only if they sit in the front
The correct child restraint for their weight
onTheTest.why: Rule 100: a child under 1.35 m must use a baby seat, child seat, booster seat or booster cushion suitable for their weight. The driver is responsible.

onTheTest.question: You want to sit in the back during your pupil's test but refuse to wear the rear seat belt. What happens?
options: You cannot accompany the test; if you won't leave, it is ended
You can stay if you hold a seat belt exemption certificate
The examiner records a fault against your pupil
You can stay, as only front seat belts are compulsory
onTheTest.why: DT1 6.29: a rear-seat passenger who refuses a seat belt, even with an exemption certificate, cannot accompany the test. If they refuse to leave, the test is terminated.

traps: A driver who is reversing, or supervising a learner who is reversing, does not need a seat belt.
Height-based child seats must face backwards until the child is over 15 months old.
Unexpected, necessary, short journey with no child seat: a child aged 3 or over can use an adult belt.
Deactivate front airbags before fitting a rear-facing baby seat in a front seat.
